 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 New Zealand's 350/9 against Australia  in 2007 is Seddon Park's highest successful ODI chase.
 Craig McMillan's 117 came after New Zealand had slipped to 41 for 4 in that pursuit of 347.
 India's 260/2 against Ireland in 2015 is the biggest chase by a visiting side at the ground.
 The highest successful run chases in ODIs at Seddon Park, Hamilton
 Seddon Park has tended to reward the side batting second, with chasing teams winning 25 of the 40 ODIs here that produced a result. Only twice, though, has a team got past 300 in the second innings at the Hamilton venue.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement CN  takes a look at the records as India go in search of a series-clinching win in the third ODI at this ground on Tuesday, November 10. They lead the five-match series 2-0 after bowling New Zealand out inside 41 overs in each of the first two games.
 India's own chasing record at Seddon Park gives them little to draw on. They have never run down a target of 250 or more against New Zealand here, and their only win in eight ODIs against the hosts came in a rain-hit game in March 2009, when they were 201 without loss.
 MORE:  Virat Kohli's record in Hamilton: How the India talisman has performed at Seddon Park in all formats 
 Highest successful ODI run chases at Seddon Park, Hamilton: Top 10 list
 The ground's biggest successful chase came on February 20, 2007, when New Zealand hauled down a target of 347 against Australia with one wicket standing and three balls to spare. Their 350 for 9 in 49.3 overs completed a 3-0 sweep of the Chappell-Hadlee series.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement New Zealand were 41 for 4 before Craig McMillan rebuilt the innings with 117 off 96 balls, striking 13 fours and five sixes. Brendon McCullum stayed with him for an unbeaten 86 off 91 balls, and Peter Fulton's 51 off 40 had given the chase its early momentum.
 Matthew Hayden still took the player of the match award for his 181 not out off 166 balls, which remains the highest individual score at the venue. His innings and Shane Watson's 68 had carried Australia to 346 for 5, a total that looked out of reach at the halfway stage. Second on the list is New Zealand's 348 for 6 against India on February 5, 2020.
 Ross Taylor made 109 not out off 84 balls, and Tom Latham 69 off 48, as the hosts overhauled 347 for 4 with 11 balls in hand, despite Shreyas Iyer's 103 and KL Rahul's 88. Those are the only 300-plus chases at Seddon Park.
 New Zealand's 290 for 7 against Bangladesh in March 2015 is next, followed by their 287 for 7 against England in February 2018 and two totals of 280 for 3 against South Africa in 2017 and India in 2014.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Visiting teams have had their moments as well. India's 260 for 2 in 36.5 overs against Ireland on March 10, 2015, is the highest chase by a touring side, while Sri Lanka's 252 for 4 beat New Zealand in January 2015, and Australia's 248 for 4 did the same in March 2010.

 The highest team totals in ODIs at Seddon Park, Hamilton: Top 10 list
 The highest total at Seddon Park belongs to a visiting side. The West Indies made 363 for 4 in 50 overs against New Zealand on January 8, 2014, and then bowled the hosts out for 160 to win by 203 runs, the heaviest defeat the ground has seen.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The next four places come from only two matches. The 2007 Chappell-Hadlee game produced New Zealand's 350 for 9 and Australia's 346 for 5, while the 2020 meeting with India gave the venue India's 347 for 4 and New Zealand's 348 for 6 in reply.
 South Africa's 339 for 4 against Zimbabwe at the 2015 World Cup is sixth, with David Miller making 138 not out off 92 balls. New Zealand's 333 for 8 against the Netherlands in April 2022 and their 292 for 8 against Pakistan in April 2025 complete the totals above 290.
